entries.proposition: Ethosuximide abolished spike-and-wave discharges in the first hour in all twelve digenic mice after systemic injection, with recurrence as the drug declined. The EEG drug experiment is in mutants only; no wild-type mouse is reported to have been dosed on the EEG endpoint.
entries.snippet: We found that SWDs were abolished in the first hour after treatment in all DiGstg+Ca1A mice (N = 12) upon systemic injection of ETX
entries.anchor: Results, Ethosuximide suppresses seizures but fails to rescue the social deficit

entries.proposition: Ethosuximide produced a broad-band reduction of cortical EEG power across frequencies, beyond SWD power, and the authors read this as an effect beyond the canonical thalamic T-type action. This is an observation of the drug's cortical-activity footprint, not a mechanistic dissection.
entries.snippet: EEG power spectrum analysis revealed broad-band cortical suppression following ETX administration, suggesting effects beyond its canonical action on thalamic T-type calcium channels (38).
entries.anchor: Discussion, Dissociation between seizures and neurocognitive behavior deficits

entries.proposition: Seizure suppression did not rescue the social-novelty deficit with ethosuximide in a repeated three-chamber design, the controls being dosed too: the group difference in social novelty (control versus digenic) was present before and after the drug. A symptomatic effect on the seizure endpoint without effect on this comorbidity.
entries.snippet: we found that ETX treatment did not rescue the social deficits in DiGstg+Ca1A mice (Fig. 2E).
entries.anchor: Results, Ethosuximide suppresses seizures but fails to rescue the social deficit

entries.proposition: Genetic ablation of Cacna1g (Cav3.1) in the digenic background removed the T-type current and rebound bursting in thalamocortical relay neurons and prevented spontaneous SWDs. This is a genetic epistasis test of T-type dependence of the seizure in the mutant, a different kind of evidence from a drug effect, and it agrees with ethosuximide.
entries.snippet: demonstrating that CaV3.1 is critical for the generation of SWDs in both monogenic and digenic absence seizure models.
entries.anchor: Results, CaV3.1 ablation prevents seizure generation

entries.proposition: The Cacna1g deletion also did not rescue social novelty, and the triple mutant still shows a trend of elevated 5 to 8 Hz power: seizures removed while cortical abnormality and the behaviour remain. The authors name this dissociation themselves and note possible effects of Cav3.1 loss on locomotion.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, peak normalized power spectra showed that TriGstg+Ca1A+Ca1G mice exhibited a trend toward elevated EEG power relative to WT controls at 5–8 Hz range (Fig. 3, G and H).
entries.anchor: Results, CaV3.1 ablation prevents seizure generation, paragraph 2; non-rescue of social novelty stated in the following paragraph

entries.proposition: The authors state the limits of the T-type conclusion: it is unclear which T-type-expressing neuron population mediates the effect, and seizure suppression should not be assumed to normalise cognitive and social outcomes.
entries.snippet: While T-type channels remain an attractive seizure-control target, these results caution against assuming that seizure suppression will normalize cognitive and social outcomes.
entries.anchor: Discussion, T-type calcium channels as a therapeutic target

entries.proposition: Figure 2 read as an image on the page render: panels B and C show SWD duration per 30 minutes collapsing from sections 1 and 2 (baseline) to near zero in sections 3 to 5, stars at 6 and 7, and no difference by section 8, i.e. the effect lasts about 2 hours and is gone by hour 4; panel D, broad drop of power with the peak near 3 Hz reduced from about 95 to about 58 microvolt squared; panel E, control (triangles, N = 17) shows social novelty before and after ETX and digenic (circles, N = 16) does not, with stars on the group difference both times; panel F, distance travelled not different between groups, before or after.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2C: sections 1-2 baseline, stars *** at sections 3-5, ** at 6-7, n.s. at 8; Figure 2D: before-ETX peak about 95, after about 58; Figure 2E: star on social-novelty group difference before and after.
entries.anchor: Figure 2 panels B to F; page 4 render at 200 dpi

entries.proposition: Figure 3 read as an image: Cacna1g-null cells lose the rebound spikes (about 5 in digenic cells, 0 in triple mutants) and the T-type current (digenic peak about 1.4 nA at -45 mV, flat at 0 in triple); EEG of the triple mutant shows no SWD; the social-novelty plot for the triple mutant versus its control carries a star (P = 0.042) while the Cacna1g-only knockout is not different from its control.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3C: bar about 5 versus 0 rebound spikes; Figure 3E: IT amplitude curve rising to about 1.4 nA versus flat at 0; Figure 3J: social-novelty bracket with a star for TriG versus Ctrl.
entries.anchor: Figure 3 panels C, E, I, J; page 5 render at 200 dpi

entries.proposition: Genetic background of the comparison: the controls named in the paper are wild type, the two single heterozygous lines and (for the triple mutant) a Cacna1g-only knockout, giving a genuine genotype ladder on the EEG endpoint; but a drug-by-genotype contrast on the EEG endpoint requires drug in more than one rung, and only the digenic rung was dosed.
entries.snippet: Phenotypic characterization compared DiGstg+Ca1A mice, Cacng2+/stg mice, Cacna1a+/− mice, and wildtype controls using video-EEG for spontaneous SWDs and power spectrum analysis.
